museum.title: Museum Conversational Guide
museum.blurb: Real-time object detection meets a RAG chatbot to give museum visitors a guide that knows what they are looking at.
description: An interactive system that moves museum visits beyond static, traditional access to information. It combines real-time object detection with a Retrieval Augmented Generation pipeline to offer a context-aware, personalised and immersive conversational guide.
Validation showed accurate spatial and conversational understanding, and a significant improvement in the veracity and relevance of the answers compared with standard LLM responses.
Published in Street Art & Urban Creativity, Vol. 11 No. 7 (2025), Special Issue: Smart City World Congress, with Álvaro Illana and Marta Salas (UFV).
Also presented on stage at the [Smart City Expo World Congress 2025](https://www.smartcityexpo.com/), the world’s leading event on urban innovation, at Fira Barcelona Gran Via.

robustBiomarkers.title: Robust Speech Biomarkers
robustBiomarkers.blurb: Keeping Parkinson’s speech biomarkers stable when a phone’s noise cancellation changes mid-study.
description: A comparative evaluation of four classifier architectures under simulated post-OS-update conditions, using the [Italian Parkinson’s Voice and Speech Dataset](https://doi.org/10.1109/MeMeA.2016.7533761). It asks whether deep-learning speech biomarkers survive a change in the operating system’s noise-cancellation algorithm during longitudinal Parkinson’s Disease monitoring.

Across six mid-study noise-cancellation change scenarios, our dual-pipeline classifier kept sensitivity within an 11.3 percentage-point spread (86.4% to 97.7%), while the three baseline architectures showed spreads of 42 to 46 points, roughly four times wider.

Selected as a poster at the [9th Annual Digital Biomarkers in Clinical Trials Summit](https://digitalbiomarkers.panagorapharma.com/) (Basel, June 2026), hosted in partnership with Roche. The evaluation used one public cohort (n = 50, 10 held-out test subjects) and software-simulated algorithms, so the results are exploratory evidence rather than direct validation against real OS updates.

The same question, applied to Alzheimer’s disease trials, was also accepted as poster P446 at [CTAD 2026 (Clinical Trials on Alzheimer’s Disease)](https://www.ctad-alzheimer.com/program-0): “Noise-cancellation variability as a source of longitudinal drift in speech-based digital endpoints for Alzheimer’s disease trials”, with Lisa Chiang (Cephalgo, Strasbourg), who presented it.
robustBiomarkers.stack: Deep Learning · Speech Biomarkers · Parkinson’s Disease

explainableAlzheimer.title: Explainable Alzheimer’s Screening
explainableAlzheimer.blurb: Screening for Alzheimer’s and mild cognitive impairment with speech features that can be traced back to what they measure.
description: Validation of fully explainable speech biomarkers for AD/MCI screening. Every feature is interpretable and traceable to a specific acoustic or linguistic construct, so a result can be explained and not only reported.

Evaluated on 44 AD/MCI cases (mean age 80.3) and 44 age-matched healthy controls (mean age 80.5), the approach reached an AUC of 0.94, with 89.3% balanced accuracy, 92.4% sensitivity and 86.3% specificity.
Accepted as an ePoster at the [AD/PD™ 2026 International Conference on Alzheimer’s and Parkinson’s Diseases](https://adpd2026.kenes.com/), with Hanyu Peng at Cephalgo SAS.
explainableAlzheimer.stack: Explainable AI · Voice Analysis · Alzheimer’s Disease

explainableParkinson.title: Explainable Parkinson’s Screening
explainableParkinson.blurb: A retrospective check that Parkinson’s can be screened from voice with features that explain themselves.
description: Validation of fully explainable speech biomarkers for PD/HC screening, the Parkinson’s counterpart of the Alzheimer’s work. Every feature is interpretable and traceable to a specific acoustic or linguistic construct.

Evaluated retrospectively on 28 Parkinson’s cases (mean age 67.2) and 37 healthy controls (mean age 48.3), the approach reached an AUC of 0.97, with 91.4% balanced accuracy, 88.5% sensitivity and 96.3% specificity. The age gap between the groups is a known imbalance of this public dataset.
Selected as an ePoster at the [AD/PD™ 2026 International Conference on Alzheimer’s and Parkinson’s Diseases](https://adpd2026.kenes.com/), with Hanyu Peng at Cephalgo SAS.
explainableParkinson.stack: Explainable AI · Voice Analysis · Parkinson’s Disease

alpaca.title: Alpaca
alpaca.blurb: A mobile app that cuts food waste at home by keeping track of what is in your pantry.
description: Alpaca (“Control En Tu Despensa”) is a mobile app for managing household food and reducing waste. It keeps a digital record of the products in the pantry, so nothing gets forgotten at the back of a shelf, expires unnoticed or ends up in the bin, and so you stop buying what you already have.

Born as a third-year university project, it was presented in the Health Informatics track of [CISTI’2024](https://web.tecnico.ulisboa.pt/~mcasquilho/ist/2024cisti-program.pdf), the 19th Iberian Conference on Information Systems and Technologies (University of Salamanca, 25–28 June 2024).
alpaca.stack: Mobile App · Food Waste · Health Informatics

kaggleStudies.title: Kaggle Studies
kaggleStudies.blurb: A handful of small but professional data-science projects.

titanic.title: Titanic
titanic.blurb: A deliberately simple XGBoost model for Kaggle’s Titanic competition, scoring 0.78.
description: My entry to the Kaggle competition [Titanic – Machine Learning from Disaster](https://www.kaggle.com/competitions/titanic): predict which passengers survived the shipwreck. The model is deliberately simple, a single XGBoost classifier, and reached a score of 0.78.
It placed 1,753rd out of 10,599 participants, which puts it in roughly the top 16.5%.

electricVehicles.title: Electric Vehicles
electricVehicles.blurb: An XGBoost model for a Kaggle Playground competition on predicting electric vehicle purchases, reaching 0.94119 AUC.
description: My entry to the Kaggle competition [Predicting Electric Vehicle Purchases](https://www.kaggle.com/competitions/playground-series-s6e9), part of the Playground Series (Season 6, Episode 9).
An XGBoost model reached an AUC of 0.94119.
